title: agents/init: add CLAUDE.md as a managed-instructions write/check target (AGENTS.md is currently the only one)
description:
Reported via opum-agent (orchestrator brief, 2026-09-05) during the one-plugin/opum-workflow fleet rebuild: the fleet's PLAN.md decision is a Claude Code-only estate with AGENTS.md retired, one memory file per repo (CLAUDE.md). opum-agent and opum-doc deleted their AGENTS.md accordingly. Consequence: `quest agents --check` now reports state: missing in both, and `quest agents --check --require-installed` (the CI form quest's own instructions tell projects to run) fails with "Quest agent instruction block is missing." There is no supported way for either repo to hold the block: quest hardcodes the write target to AGENTS.md with no CLAUDE.md option and no opt-out.

Confirmed by direct source read (not relayed): `codexInstructionPath = "AGENTS.md"` (src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts:9) is the sole default, threaded unchanged through `updateQuestAgentInstructions`/`inspectQuestAgentInstructions` (same file, lines 78-95), and every call site (`quest agents --check`/`--update-instructions` at src/cli/main.ts:858-859, `quest init --agent-instructions` at src/cli/main.ts:747) omits the path argument, so it is always AGENTS.md. Neither the `agents` command (`--check`, `--require-installed`, `--update-instructions` only) nor `init` (`--agent-instructions`, `--name`, `--task-id-prefix`, `--reconfigure` only) exposes any target/path flag. `workspace.toml` has no field for it either (src/application/workspaces/workspaces.ts:41-46). The only thing that already generalizes is the internal `AgentInstructionPort.read/write(path)` interface (src/ports/agent-instructions.ts), which accepts an arbitrary relative path but is never given anything but the AGENTS.md default.

lore-cli hit the identical gap today during its own rebuild and correctly HELD its AGENTS.md deletion rather than become a third broken repo (its finding: LCLI-442). lore already writes its own nudge block to CLAUDE.md and couples its Codex bridge to AGENTS.md's presence (deleting AGENTS.md is the supported way to drop Codex for lore) - that CLAUDE.md-target capability is exactly what quest lacks.

quest-cli is a published package (@opum-ai/quest) with external users, not only this fleet's internal tool - QCLI-159 (still To Do) already flags that Codex/AGENTS.md support is real shipped product surface, not something the fleet can retire unilaterally. So the fix here should be additive (a new CLAUDE.md target, explicitly selected), not a default-target flip that would silently stop writing AGENTS.md for existing external Codex-only callers. QCLI-159 already scopes a broader multi-select ("which agent instruction file(s) to write": Claude Code -> CLAUDE.md, Codex -> AGENTS.md, pi -> TBD) but is unimplemented and bundles in unrelated UX/wizard and "pi" identification questions. This task narrows to the piece actually blocking the fleet right now: give CLAUDE.md a real, checkable write target, without waiting on QCLI-159's fuller design.

Scope: the write/check target selection only. Not in scope: the interactive wizard UX, the "pi" agent identity question, or removing AGENTS.md support from the product.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest agents --update-instructions (and the quest init agent-instructions path) can write the managed quest:agent-instructions block to CLAUDE.md, instead of or in addition to AGENTS.md, via an explicit selection (flag or workspace config) - not a silent default-target change

quest agents --check and --check --require-installed validate against whichever target(s) were actually configured/written for the workspace, so a CLAUDE.md-only repo (no AGENTS.md at all) can report state: current and pass --require-installed
Existing --agent-instructions boolean flag and the unflagged default (AGENTS.md) are unchanged for callers who pass no new flag, so external/published-package Codex-only callers are not broken

Relationship to QCLI-159 is recorded explicitly: whether this task's CLAUDE.md target lands as a narrow first step QCLI-159 later builds its multi-select UX on top of, or QCLI-159 is revised to absorb it - not built in parallel contradiction
Tests cover a CLAUDE.md-only target end to end (write, check, require-installed all pass with no AGENTS.md present) and confirm the default unflagged path is unchanged

implementationNotes: Implemented: agentInstructionPathForTarget(target?: 'claude'|'codex') in src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts resolves to the existing codexInstructionPath (AGENTS.md, default) or new claudeInstructionPath (CLAUDE.md). Wired a --target flag onto 'agents --check'/'--update-instructions' and 'init --agent-instructions' in src/cli/main.ts; --target requires --agent-instructions on init (usage error otherwise) and rejects any value other than claude/codex. No workspace.toml schema change - explicit per-invocation flag, not persisted config, since the caller (CI script or init wizard) already knows its own target. Port layer (LocalAgentInstructionPort) already supported arbitrary relative paths with symlink/escape guards, so no adapter change was needed. Default/unflagged behavior verified byte-identical: the full existing test suite (403 tests) passes unchanged except two help-text assertions intentionally updated for the new --target flag documentation.

AC3 (QCLI-159 relationship): recorded a cross-reference note on QCLI-159 earlier confirming this task lands as a narrow, additive first step - the flag-based --target selection and agentInstructionPathForTarget resolver - which QCLI-159's broader interactive multi-select wizard and unresolved 'pi' target question can build on rather than duplicate. Not built in contradiction: QCLI-159 remains To Do for the richer UX.
finalSummary: Added CLAUDE.md as a real, checkable managed-instructions target alongside AGENTS.md, unblocking opum-agent and opum-doc's 'agents --check --require-installed' CI now that both deleted AGENTS.md per the fleet's Claude-Code-only decision. New --target claude|codex flag on 'quest init --agent-instructions' and 'quest agents --check|--update-instructions' (default omitted = codex/AGENTS.md, byte-identical to prior behavior - verified by the full pre-existing suite passing unchanged). Each invocation targets exactly one file; writing both is two invocations, not new combined-output logic, matching the narrow scope agreed for this task versus QCLI-159's fuller multi-select design. New test coverage: CLAUDE.md-only end-to-end (write/check/require-installed all pass with zero AGENTS.md ever created), the other target correctly reporting missing, drift detection under --target claude, and usage-error coverage for --target without --agent-instructions and an invalid --target value. Command help (quest help agents/init) documents the new flag. Full bun run check green: typecheck, lint (2 pre-existing unrelated warnings), format, layer boundaries, 403/403 tests.
